children: While Indonesia's August inflation remains within Bank Indonesia's target range, the central bank is likely to remain cautious, balancing the need to support growth against inflation and rupiah stability risks, UOB economist Enrico Tanuwidjaja says in a note. Price pressures continue to stem from food, gold jewelry and transport, while Middle East tensions remain the key upside risk through higher energy, logistics and transport costs, he says. Inflation is projected to average around 2.5% in 2026 before rising to 3.0% in 2027, driven by firmer domestic demand and the normalization of administered and services prices, he adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
